judgments.reasoning_cat1: The acknowledgment ends with an open catch-all, "other material provided by NOLS describing or related to my program," whose reach is undefined, and "has been available to more fully explain" is a vague representation rather than a definite obligation. That general-vs-specific structure after the enumerated Catalog, Admission Policies, Risk Management statement and Enrollment Packet leaves genuine scope uncertainty.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read against the "Activities and Risks" bullets and the Assumption of Risks paragraph, this clause functions as a purported incorporation of extrinsic documents that are nowhere else identified or attached, which could put it in tension with the integration-style closing statement that the agreement comprises four pages and may be modified only in writing. That tension is real but modest.
judgments.clause_name: Activities and Risks — Acknowledgment of Reading NOLS Materials

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[A]ny mediation or suit shall occur or be filed only in the State of Wyoming" is the classic ambiguity between a geographic designation (any court sitting in Wyoming, including federal) and a sovereign designation (Wyoming state courts only); the stray asterisk and the garbled parenthetical about "the laws which might apply the laws of another jurisdiction" add mechanical defects. A court would have something concrete to construe in the words "in the State of Wyoming."
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing else in the document addresses venue or dispute resolution, so there is no competing forum provision; the severability clause coexists with it without conflict. The only mild friction is that the release contemplates suits by third parties who never signed, but that is not a direct contradiction.
judgments.clause_name: Other Provisions — Governing Law and Forum Selection

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The recital that the signers "HAVE READ THIS PAGE AND THE PREVIOUS 3 PAGES" is a page-count reference that can misdescribe the actual document, and "BINDING UPON THEM, THEIR HEIRS, ESTATE, EXECUTORS AND ADMINISTRATORS" raises a scope question about whether non-signing heirs' independent claims are captured. The enumerated list of successors with no catch-all also invites an expressio unius argument.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be squared with the release and indemnity paragraph, which separately addresses claims by "a member of my family, a rescuer, another student, or any other person," and with the preamble's conditional parent-signature requirement; the binding-on-heirs language overlaps rather than plainly conflicts. Some tension exists over whether a parent can bind a minor's own claims, but the provisions can be harmonised.
judgments.clause_name: Final Provision — Binding on Heirs, Estate, Executors and Administrators

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[U]nder 18 years of age in most states" and the instruction that "Student and parent must determine the age of legal competency" are hedged and shift a legal determination to the signers, leaving the definitional boundary of "minor" soft. The definitional caveat "unless indicated otherwise" is also unspecific, though the operative signature requirement itself is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is consistent with the later paragraphs that repeatedly condition obligations on "if I am an adult student, or the parent of a minor student," and with the signature block calling for a parent signature only for minors. No contradicting provision was found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The list of activities is expressly non-exhaustive ("include, among others"), and "inherent risks" is given a definition, so the drafting anticipates and defuses the usual scope objection. "Unique character of the activities" is somewhat vague but is a stated definitional device rather than an operative trigger.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It dovetails with the Acknowledgment and Assumption paragraph, which repeats that the description "is not complete," so the two are coherent. No conflicting provision identified.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line, purely descriptive statement of risk; "strenuous" is imprecise but nothing operative turns on its boundary. There is no list or catch-all to construe.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Descriptive and hedged ("usually," "may be many days"), but it imposes no duty, so the vagueness has no operative bite. Nothing here needs construing.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A four-word factual statement with no ambiguous operative term and no enumeration. Definite on its face.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Camping risks include" is an open list, and "offending food types" is loose, but as a descriptive risk disclosure nothing operative hinges on the list's outer edge. Low textual risk.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[F]orces of nature" and "other mild or serious conditions" are catch-alls appended to specific hazards, but again the sentence only illustrates rather than allocates. Modest scope softness only.
